changes.before: Replace continue with break. What prints?
changes.after: Repeat with a counter and skip one turn.

before: for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) declares a counter once, checks the condition before each body run, and increments after each completed body. i++ increases i by one.
continue skips the rest of the current body. In a for loop, its update still runs before the next condition check.
break exits the loop immediately. It is different from continue, which starts another loop cycle if the condition permits.
Follow initialization, test, body, update, then test again. A value skipped by continue does not cause the counter to stop changing.
Expected behavior from this example: 0, 2, and 3 on separate lines. This expected result is a reasoned prediction until a compiler test is recorded.

Optional local transfer task: Predict output when the skipped value changes to 2. Then compare continue with break at that same value. You may trace it on paper if no C# toolchain is installed; reading completion does not certify a run.
after: A for loop repeats code. Its first part sets up a counter once. Here, i starts at zero.
The middle part checks whether another turn is allowed. i < 4 allows a turn only while i is less than four.
The final part runs after each completed turn. i++ adds one to i. Then the loop checks its condition again.
continue skips the rest of the current turn. In this for loop, i++ still runs, so the counter keeps moving.
The program prints 0, 2, and 3 on separate lines. At 1, continue skips the print. At 4, the condition stops the loop.
break leaves the loop immediately. Unlike continue, it does not move on to another turn of this loop.
